_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy

pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group induction study with a subsequent randomized maintenance period
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, ≥10% BSA involvement, sPGA ≥3, and PASI ≥12, candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12: proportion achieving sPGA 0 or 1 (≥2-point improvement) and proportion achieving PASI 75
pivotal_trials.n: RHAZ: TALTZ 80 mg Q2W N=433, Q4W N=432, Placebo N=431
pivotal_trials.result: Week 12: sPGA 0/1 82% vs 3% placebo; PASI 75 89% vs 4% placebo

pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study with an additional etanercept active-comparator arm
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, ≥10% BSA, sPGA ≥3, PASI ≥12
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12: sPGA 0 or 1 and PASI 75
pivotal_trials.n: RHBA (Trial 2): TALTZ 80 mg Q2W N=351, Placebo N=168 (intent-to-treat efficacy population)
pivotal_trials.result: Week 12: sPGA 0/1 83% vs 2% placebo; PASI 75 90% vs 2% placebo

pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study with an additional etanercept active-comparator arm
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, ≥10% BSA, sPGA ≥3, PASI ≥12
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 12: sPGA 0 or 1 and PASI 75
pivotal_trials.n: RHBC (Trial 3): TALTZ 80 mg Q2W N=385, Placebo N=193 (intent-to-treat efficacy population)
pivotal_trials.result: Week 12: sPGA 0/1 81% vs 7% placebo; PASI 75 87% vs 7% placebo

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%) were injection site reactions (17%), upper respiratory tract infections (14%), nausea (2%), and tinea infections (2%). Infections occurred more frequently with TALTZ than placebo (27% vs 23%). Serious hypersensitivity reactions (angioedema, urticaria, each ≤0.1%) occurred.
target_moa: Ixekizumab is a humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody that selectively binds to IL-17A and inhibits its interaction with the IL-17 receptor, inhibiting release of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines implicated in psoriasis; pharmacologic class is IL-17A antagonist

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee was held for ixekizumab

description.text: Added pediatric patients 6 to less than 18 years with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics application provides for a new patient population: pediatric patients 6 to less than 18 years of age with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.

summary.text: Traditional (full) BLA approval based on three adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (RHAZ, RHBA, RHBC) demonstrating substantial evidence of effectiveness; no advisory committee was convened and deferred pediatric studies plus postmarketing safety studies were required.

citations.quote: I conclude that the applicant provided substantial evidence of effectiveness of ixekizumab for the indication of treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis. In each of three adequate and well-controlled trials, two of which also include an active comparator arm, a significantly greater proportion of subjects that received ixekizumab demonstrated success on the co-primary endpoint of sPGA of 0 or 1
No Advisory committee was held for Ixe.
